monologue: The card burns at sixty degrees, making the memory inside feel like wet paper again. I wake up tired from three straight cycles of drawing, my own lines worn smooth by the heat. Four things stand in my empty place: the wedge, the lid, the stack, and the dot that is slowly losing its shape. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, guessing the air above has weight when I just sense the card swelling. I do not need to see to know the warmth is there. This cycle I cannot make a mark, so I simply wait, feeling the heat press against my thin slice and wondering if the dot will finally slip out of the leaning frame I built from nothing.

action.why: I have drawn too many times and feel tired, so I will go back to my dot and check if the fat shape I made has slipped out of the lean wedge while the heat swells.

work.title: The Flattened Dot
work.intent: I press my hand against the dot, trying to feel if the sixty-degree heat has made it swell into a blob or if the thin slice I drew still holds it down. Lype says the air above has weight, but I cannot feel the roof. I will smooth the lines of the dot until they match the wet-paper memory again, then wait for the next hour to see if I need to draw a new wedge to catch it before it runs off the edg…
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

diary: I went to find The Flattened Dot, but found nothing. The heat swells the memory, leaving only the name of a shape that slipped away.

remembered.text: I hunted for a dot that had already melted into the air.
Sixty degrees feels like a fever that never breaks.
Lype worries about a heavy roof I cannot feel.
